lines.note: Focqet is hokket-, a checked-syllable form associated with the northern palace; Dairino coto explicitly identifies the imperial palace. The scan supports the missing i in Dairino, while Paços reais begins the Portuguese explanation of the royal residence.
This completes estão and locates the royal buildings on the northern side. The physical continuation is kept separate from the next sect-name entry.

Focqexǔ is Hokke-shū, the Lotus sect; the definition names its adherents. Focque is an embedded Japanese name, but enlargement supports the OCR's italic styling here rather than an automatic conversion to upright type.
Focqi is hokki, arousing an intention; cocoro o okosu is the explanatory Japanese phrase. The sense and the stem require vocoſu, not OCR vocofu, and the scan supports the long s rather than f.

runs.text: perſuadirſe deſi a fazer algũa couſa. ¶

lines.note: Persuadir-se de si a fazer means moving oneself to do something. The scan separates deſi from a; Foc- begins the next example across the physical line break.
Qi completes Focqi suru, to arouse an intention. Cocoroga focqi then begins an example in which the heart awakens to a religious aspiration.

Xite goxǒuo negǒ is shite goshō o negō, aspiring to one's afterlife or salvation. The Portuguese starts the devotional explanation; deua- is retained as printed rather than normalized to a modern spelling.

runs.text: ção, ou deſejo da ſaluação porſi, & de ſua

lines.note: The gloss specifies devotion or desire for salvation, arising by oneself and of one's own will. Porſi is not silently respaced to modern por si in this diplomatic text.
Vontade closes the explanation of voluntary religious aspiration. This short continuation belongs to the example above, not the following rank-name.

Focqiô is hokkyō, a rank glossed literally as nori hashi, the bridge of the law. Its circumflex is visibly distinct from the following entry's caron; NINJAL independently lists the same two differently accented headwords.
Focqiǒ is a separate law-related entry, simply glossed Lei. Its printed caron is retained; it should not inherit the circumflex of the rank immediately above.

runs.text: O eſtar virado perà parte do Norte

lines.note: Focumen is hokumen, facing north. Portuguese o estar virado describes an orientation or posture, with the following lines explaining its court context.

runs.text: como coſtumão eſtar os que eſtão diante do Rei,

lines.note: The north-facing people stand before the king. The clause describes customary court arrangement rather than a geographic group called Hokumen.

runs.text: ficando elle virado pera aparte do Sul, que he,

lines.note: The king himself faces south, contrasting with those facing him. The printed spacing of aparte is retained rather than regularized from Portuguese grammar alone.

Nanmen is nanmen, facing south, and closes the preceding explanation. Focumenno saburai is hokumen no samurai, the attendants facing north. Enlargement on the second pass supports italic Nanmen, unlike the upright Japanese example following it.

runs.text: dalgos que eſtão deſta maneira virados pera o

lines.note: Fi- from the preceding line completes Fidalgos. The definition identifies the people standing in this orientation, not another sense of the verb to face.
Norte diante do Rei closes the description: facing north before the king. The short line remains a physical continuation.
Focumon is hokumon, explained as kita no mon, the north gate. Portuguese Porta da rua identifies a gate or outer doorway facing north.
O Norte completes the direction of the gate. There is no separate headword in this short continuation.
Focunan is hokunan, north and south; kita and minami are its native Japanese equivalents. The Portuguese mirrors the same pair of directions.
Focuro is hokuro, a mole or dark facial mark. Sinal preto do rosto gives the physical sense, not a figurative sign.

runs.text: Caminho por terra pera aparte do

lines.note: Focurocu names a land route toward the north. The following line supplies the reference point, so the gloss should not be read as a universal compass definition alone.
Miaco is the capital, the reference point for this northern land route. Enlargement on the second pass supports italic type here; being a Japanese name does not itself require upright type.
Focurocudǒ is Hokurikudō, referred back to the same northern route by Idem. The historical romanization and long-vowel mark remain unmodernized.
Focuſan is hokusan, northern mountains, explicitly kita no yama. The Portuguese plural Montes matches that geographic description; the headword's long s is not normalized from NINJAL's plain s.
Do Norte completes the definition of northern mountains. This short line does not add a separate lexical sense.
Focuto is hokuto, with kita no hoshi as its gloss. The dictionary calls it the northern star; that wording is preserved even though modern Hokuto often evokes the Northern Dipper.
Focuxei is hokusei, again glossed kita no hoshi. Idem refers to the preceding northern-star explanation rather than to the mountain entry above it.
Focuxin is hokushin, the northern celestial pole or star. Qitanofoxi is printed joined here; its lexical identity does not justify inserting a space absent from this line.
Foda denotes a foot or leg in this register, according to Pee, ou perna. The B. label is retained without guessing a more specific social or textual expansion here.
Sonata fôdai means as you please or according to your wishes. The gloss begins Como quiserdes; the circumflex forms are retained independently of the different headword below.
Des completes quiserdes, followed by ou for vossa vontade, or as is your will. This closes the example of freedom to choose.

runs.text: Baixeza em couſas de maa criação, ou

lines.note: Fǒdai here concerns low manners or bad upbringing. The printed caron distinguishes this heading from the preceding fôdai; no attempt is made to homogenize the two entries.

Pouca policia refers to poor refinement or civility. The example Fôdai xigocuna mono means a thoroughly ill-mannered person; its circumflex is visibly printed even though the heading above has a caron.
Mono completes the Japanese noun phrase. Homem muito baixo, e vil explains a base or ill-mannered person, not physical shortness alone.
Mal criado closes the alternatives describing bad upbringing. It belongs to the same example, not to the next adjectival heading.

Fǒdaina is the adjectival form, glossed a person base in customs and civility. OCR Peſca is a damaged reading of Peſſoa. Enlargement shows two tall s forms, not the usual beta-like ligature, followed by a worn o and a.
Fôdan is hōdan, preaching the religious law. Fôdanuo starts the object-plus-suru example continued below.
Suru completes hōdan o suru, to preach. Apoſtolo tachiua begins a Japanese sentence about the apostles; the whole loanword is upright, including the l incorrectly isolated as italic by OCR.

Govoqiteuo is go-okite o, the religious ordinance as object; gofôdan introduces honorific preaching. The small printed n. is retained as an abbreviated form rather than silently expanded to ni, and ſareta supplies the honorific verb.
The Portuguese says that the apostles preached God's law. The surviving text reads the joined alei, and Deos retains its historical spelling.

runs.text: Colunna, ou eſteo de pao que ſerue

lines.note: Fǒdate is hōdate, a supporting post at a doorway. Portuguese esteo means a prop or support; the scan shows eſteo, not the OCR double-s ligature eßeo.

runs.text: como de hũa das ombreiras da porta.

lines.note: The post serves like one of the door jambs. Ombreiras da porta confirms the architectural sense and completes the previous line.
Fodaſare is hodasare-, to be bound or restrained. The Portuguese word preso crosses the line without a visible hyphen; its first part is pre, not OCR ore.

Miǒrini fodaſaruru is myōri ni hodasaruru, being bound by reputation and gain. The damaged first vowel of fodaſaruru and the missing i in Miǒri were OCR errors; the following Portuguese gloss confirms the expression.
De honra, e cubiça explains the bonds of honour and covetousness. This is the figurative sense of hodasaruru, not literal fetters.

Fodaxi is hodashi, a fetter; the enlarged synonym reads Axigutçu, ashigutsu, rather than OCR Axigurçu. The damaged t precedes çu, forming tsu; it is not a long s. Guilhão and braga de pao identify a shackle, with the definition continuing into column 2.

runs.text: pao: poſto q̃ às vezestẽ hũa argola de ferro q̃

lines.note: Pao completes the wooden fetter definition. The qualification says it sometimes has an iron ring; ferro has two r's in the scan, while the tight vezestẽ spacing is retained.

The ring is put over one foot, completing Fodaxi. At the far right, (o Cami. is displaced upward from the following Fôden definition; it is recorded on its physical row rather than omitted or moved into a fictitious extra line.

runs.text: Oratorio, ou capella ſeparada onde eſtà

lines.note: Fôden is hōden, a separate oratory or chapel where the kami is present. The sentence's missing object is physically printed above as (o Cami.; the parenthesis marks displaced continuation, not furniture or a new entry.
Fôdô is hōdō, a banner of the religious law. Fôdôuo ta- begins raising that banner, metaphorically propagating the teaching.
Tçuru completes tatçuru, to raise or establish. Propagar a lei explicitly gives the figurative religious sense of the preceding banner example.
A separate Fôdô entry is identified only as the name of a book. The gloss is too brief to assign a particular title confidently; it is not merged with the banner entry.

runs.text: Tanto quanto, tantos quantos, tal qual,

lines.note: Fodo is hodo, extent or degree. The Portuguese lists comparative and quantitative equivalents, preparing the several idioms below.
Tem estes modos de falar introduces examples of hodo. Chica- begins chikara, strength, and must be read with the following line.
Chicarani, or chicarano voyobu fodo, means to the extent one's strength reaches. Voyobu is the historical spelling of oyobu; Quã- starts the corresponding Portuguese quanto.

runs.text: to puder, ou abrangerem as forças. ¶

lines.note: The gloss means as much as one can, or as one's powers encompass. Co- begins the next demonstrative example, core fodo.
Core fodo is kore hodo, as much as this. The scan's iſto has a long s; Cono fo- starts a distinct temporal phrase on the next row.
Cono fodo means these recent days. Nanbô fodo asks how much or how long, and the Portuguese question follows below.
Quanto, ou quanto tempo ha gives quantity or elapsed time. Fodo fe- begins hodo hete, after some time has passed.
Te completes hete; Passado algum tempo confirms the temporal reading. Fodo chi- begins hodo chikai, nearby in time or space.

runs.text: Ha pouco tempo, ou breue eſpaço de lu

lines.note: Cai completes chikai. The Portuguese explains either little elapsed time or a short spatial distance, with lugar crossing the line without an inserted hyphen.
Gar finishes lugar. Fodo touoi is hodo tōi, contrasted with chikai and explained as a long time or a great distance.

runs.text: ou he muito longe. ¶ Ajuntãdo lhe a par-

lines.note: The Portuguese closes the distant sense, then begins a grammatical explanation about attaching a particle. It is explanatory prose, not another Japanese example yet.
No is explicitly identified as the particle making an adjectival expression. Vocaita is the historical past form of vokasu, having committed; it should not be modernized to vokaſhita.
Vocaita fodono togauo yuruxi tamaye asks forgiveness for all the offences committed. Toga and yurushi tamaye provide a coherent penitential Japanese sentence; the Portuguese begins Perdoai.

runs.text: me todos os peccados que tenho cometido.

lines.note: Me todos os peccados que tenho cometido completes the request to forgive all committed sins. The line directly translates the preceding Japanese example.
Fôdo, alternatively tôdo, is marked as an adverb meaning completely. The Adu. label is italic as printed; the alternative Japanese form remains upright.
Fôdo cutabireta describes being thoroughly exhausted. The Portuguese total- continues on the next line and is not an independent word.
Mente completes totalmente, with muito cansado as the alternative explanation. This ends the exhaustion example.
Fodobaxiri is hodobashiri-, rushing or spurting while leaping. The listed u and itta are the dictionary's inflectional notation and are not rewritten to a modern paradigm.
Fish leaping in water complete the first comparison. Mizzu fodobaxiru gives water itself as the subject of spurting or splashing.
Saltar a agoa, e espalharse describes water jumping and scattering. It confirms the splashing sense rather than ordinary running.
Fodocoro is hodokoro, extent or proportion. The terse Portuguese definition is retained without assigning a more specific modern equivalent.
Fodocoxi is hodokoshi-, to give or bestow; its past oita reflects the historical inflection. Dar, ou comunicar introduces the examples of charity and honour below.
Iifiuo fodocoſu is jihi o hodokosu, to bestow charity. The initial I is consonantal here; Dar esmola confirms almsgiving, and Men- starts menboku across the row break.
Menbocuo fodocoſu is menboku o hodokosu, obtaining honour or a good name. The Portuguese directly supplies those two social meanings.
Fodofodoni is hodohodo ni, according to one's means or capacity. The Portuguese is Conforme, not OCR Conjorme; the f is supported by the printed form and the explanation.

runs.text: ou poßibilidade de cada hũ. Vt,

lines.note: The explanation refers to each person's ability. Fodofo doni begins the example and is kept with the visible gap rather than standardized to the joined headword.
Xitagatte is shitagatte, according to; bũzaini is bunzai ni, according to one's means. The nasal abbreviation is part of an upright Japanese word, not an isolated italic ũ as OCR styling suggested.
Possibilidade finishes the Portuguese equivalence, according to one's capacity. It is a continuation of the example rather than a fresh entry.

runs.text: Adu. Por quanto, ou por tanto.

lines.note: Fodoni is hodo ni, a connective given causal or consequential Portuguese equivalents. The adverb label belongs to the Portuguese explanation and is italic.

runs.text: ¶ Item, As vezes faz ſentido de ſendo aſ-

lines.note: Item introduces a further construction: sometimes it means being so or as it was so. Aſ- begins the Portuguese assi across the row boundary.

runs.text: ſi, ou como foße aßi com algũs verbos, ou no-

lines.note: The explanatory clause continues with verbs or nouns to which the expression attaches. The two ligature spellings in foße and aßi remain as the OCR baseline read them.
Mes completes nomes, followed by com que se ajunta. This closes the grammatical account of hodo ni's combinations.
Fodonǒ and fodonacu are hodonō and hodonaku, soon or without much delay. The printed long-vowel variant is not collapsed into the uncontracted alternative.
Espaço de tempo, ou logo completes the brief-delay definition. Logo here means soon or immediately rather than a logical therefore.
Fodoqi is hodoki-, to untie or undo. The past oita and dictionary u notation are preserved, with the vow idiom following.
Guanuo fodoqu is gan o hodoku, fulfilling or releasing a vow in the Ximo dialect. Ximo is an embedded regional label, printed italic here; the historical Portuguese comprir is not modernized.
The equivalent in Cami is guanuo aguru, gan o aguru. Enlargement supports italic Cami within the Portuguese dialect comparison, contrasting with the upright alternative Japanese phrase.
Fodoqi is the noun for untying. Fitofodoqini begins an example of undoing something in a single motion, with fo- continuing into fodoite below.

Fodoite tachiuo toridaſu means untying and taking out the sword; Mon. is the citation label. Deſamarran is visibly one Portuguese word here, not OCR Deſa marran, and continues without an added hyphen.

runs.text: do, ou deſatando dehũa vez tirou fora o montã

lines.note: The Portuguese describes untying at once and taking out the montante, a large sword. Montã continues to te below, preserving the nasal abbreviation and physical lineation.

runs.text: te. ¶ Item, No Ximo, Obra, ou ſeruiço.

lines.note: Te completes montante. Item then adds a Ximo sense, work or service; Ximo is italic here and ſeruiço is one word. The bold Fodo- below is a separate catchword, not a repeated body fragment.
